summary: Arthur Woollgar Verrall studied at Wellington College (~1864–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1874). He later taught Robert Alexander Neil.

Arti Dhand is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Calgary and McGill University. Around 2002, she served as Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto.
Aruna Haldar worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Girindrasekhar Bose and Kedarnath Ojha, and later held a teaching post at Patna University.

Indologist Arunoday Natvarlal Jani earned his Ph.D. under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt at the University of Mumbai (~1946–1953) and studied at M.S. University of Baroda. He served as Senior Lecturer at Baroda (1967–1980) and Director of the Oriental Institute (1975–1981).

Scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy Arvind Sharma studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard universities. He held posts at the University of Queensland (1976), University of Sydney (1980), and McGill University as Birks Chair in Comparative Religion (1994).

Buddhist studies figure Aryadeva studied under Nagarjuna and Shakyamitra. He was associated with the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning and taught numerous pupils, including Candrakīrti, Tilopa, and Shakyamitra.

Asanga Tilakaratne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the University of Kelaniya's Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, he served as Head of Buddhist Thought and Professor, and later as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Asatoshi Kamiya, active in Buddhist studies, received an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). He later worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin High School (attested 1978).

Asen Balikci was a scholar of history and archaeology who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1956. He held posts at the National Museum of Canada (~1957–1968) and the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

Ashok Aklujkar, an Indology, linguistics, and philosophy scholar, studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and completed his PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1965–1970). He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

Ashok Kumar Chatterjee earned his degrees in philosophy under T. R. V. Murti at Banaras Hindu University. He headed the philosophy department at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) before serving as professor and department head at BHU (1963–1985).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at the East-West Center (~1963–1967). He founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

Linguist and Indologist Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University (~1956–1958). He held positions at Pune, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and Deccan College (~1967–1989) as Professor of Applied Linguistics and Centre Director.

Ashutosh Mukherjee studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served at the Calcutta High Court (1904), as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1906–1914, 1921–1923), and as President of The Asiatic Society (~1907–1915).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee, an Indology and history/archaeology scholar, completed his Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta (~1964–1967). He served as a Senior Research Fellow at Calcutta (attested 1970) and lecturer at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Pentti Aalto, whom he later succeeded, as well as R. Panneerselvam and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies and University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Archaeologist Astley John Hilary Goodwin studied at Selwyn College (1919–1922) and SOAS University of London (1922). He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923 and taught Bridget Allchin.

Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Leipzig. She has held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).
Athanaric Huard, active in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. He held a post as Assistent at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei and Tokyo universities, Strasbourg, EPHE, and under Georges Dumézil. Specializing in religious studies and history/archaeology, he worked at CNRS (~1964–1969) and held professorships at Seikei University (1970) and Gakushuin University (2006).
